candidates.label: Nicopolis archaeological site (Epirus)
candidates.support: Several cities in antiquity were named Nicopolis ('victory city'); OpenBible.info's identification for Titus 3:12 resolves to this Nicopolis in Epirus, northwestern Greece, which Augustus founded to commemorate his naval victory at nearby Actium. Pleiades and Wikidata's coordinates for the site agree closely.

summary.text: Nicopolis in Epirus was founded by Augustus (then Octavian) to commemorate his victory over Mark Antony and Cleopatra at the nearby Battle of Actium in 31 BC. Paul's letter to Titus asks Titus to join him at Nicopolis, where Paul had decided to spend the winter.

history.text: Augustus founded Nicopolis, near his former camp, as the largest of the monuments built to commemorate his victory at Actium in 31 BC.

scripture.textWEB: When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, be diligent to come to me to Nicopolis, for I have determined to winter there.
